q: מטופל בן 87 עם דמנציה מתקדמת הוגדר בישראל כחולה הנוטה למות שאינו בעל כשרות. אין ביד הצוות הנחיות מקדימות, ובן זוגו מבקש להימנע מטיפול אך טרם מסר מה היה רצון המטופל. מה נדרש לברר?
o: את רצון בן הזוג ביחס לסדרי הטיפול.
את הערכת הצוות לגבי השגרה המתאימה.
את רצון המטופל מתוך מסמכים ועדות אדם קרוב.
את עמדת המשפחה לגבי המשך הביקורים.
explanation:
**יש לברר את רצון החולה עצמו באמצעות ההנחיות או ההחלטות הרלוונטיות, ובהיעדרן באמצעות הצהרת אדם קרוב לפי החוק.**

**א. את רצון בן הזוג ביחס לסדרי הטיפול** — בן זוג עשוי למסור עדות על רצון המטופל. העדפתו האישית של בן הזוג אינה רצון המטופל.
**ב. את הערכת הצוות לגבי השגרה המתאימה** — שגרת המחלקה אינה עדות לרצון החולה.
**ג. את רצון המטופל מתוך מסמכים ועדות אדם קרוב** — בודקים מסמכים והנחיות ופונים לאדם קרוב כדי לברר את הרצון הידוע של המטופל.
**ד. את עמדת המשפחה לגבי המשך הביקורים** — עומס הביקורים עשוי להיות נושא לתמיכה במשפחה, אך אינו קובע את רצונו של החולה.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיפים 5(ב)–5(ג) ו־9.

q: An 81-year-old woman with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction takes spironolactone. Repeated testing shows hyperkalemia and significant renal dysfunction, with creatinine 2.7 mg/dL. Which decision about mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists is supported by Hazzard?
o: Continue spironolactone at the current dose to preserve its heart-failure benefit
Stop spironolactone for the contraindication and monitor potassium and renal function
Substitute eplerenone to preserve treatment with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
Increase spironolactone to strengthen the diuretic effect of her treatment
explanation:
Spironolactone improves outcomes in suitable patients with HFrEF, but impaired potassium excretion can make it unsafe. **Hold it and reassess potassium and renal function** when repeated testing shows hyperkalemia with significant renal dysfunction.

**A. Continue at the same dose** Benefit in eligible patients does not remove the immediate risk in this patient.
**B. Stop and monitor** Reconfirm severity and manage hyperkalemia while reviewing renal function and other potassium-raising drugs.
**C. Switch to eplerenone** It is more selective at the receptor but shares the potassium-retaining effect.
**D. Increase spironolactone** Greater blockade can aggravate hyperkalemia and is unsafe as a way to intensify diuresis here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1181.

q: A patient has new symptomatic high-grade AV block with hemodynamic compromise after TAVR. Emergency stabilization is complete, but the block persists. What should be arranged before discharge?
o: Ambulatory monitoring as the sole intervention
Permanent pacemaker implantation during this admission
Elective pacing only if bundle-branch block recurs
Routine discharge once the blood pressure normalizes
explanation:
Persistent symptomatic or hemodynamically significant post-TAVR AV block warrants permanent pacing before discharge. Isolated bundle-branch block without high-grade AV block requires a different monitoring strategy.

**A. Ambulatory monitoring as the sole intervention** — Observation alone does not treat persistent symptomatic high-grade block.
**B. Permanent pacemaker implantation during this admission** — The persistent hemodynamically significant block is the indication for pacing.
**C. Elective pacing only if bundle-branch block recurs** — A separate bundle-branch finding is not required.
**D. Routine discharge once the blood pressure normalizes** — Temporary improvement in pressure does not demonstrate recovery of conduction.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p1200; ACC/AHA/HRS bradycardia guideline, §8.1.2.4.

q: גבר בן 78 עם סוכרת, neuropathy פריפרית, ודמנציה קלה מסוג אלצהיימר (MMSE 20) מגיע לטיפול דחוף עקב זיהום ברגל. אשתו, המטפלת העיקרית שלו, הביאה אותו לאחר שעוזרת הבית הביעה דאגה. בבדיקה: אצבע רגל נקרוטית עם ריח רע ודלף מוגלתי, ומספר אזורים נוספים של פירוק רקמות בשתי הרגליים. האישה אומרת: 'אני בודקת את הרגליים שלו כל יום כמו שאמרו לי.' ה-HbA1c של המטופל הוא 11.8%. איזה היבט מצביע בצורה החזקה ביותר על caregiver neglect?
o: זיהום ברגל אצל מטופל הסובל גם מנוירופתיה סוכרתית
פער בין דיווח המטפלת לממצאים החמורים בבדיקת הרגל
סוכרת שאינה מאוזנת אצל מטופל עם ליקוי קוגניטיבי
זיהוי הבעיה בידי עוזרת הבית ולא בידי האישה
explanation:
**פער בולט בין הדיווח על בדיקה יומית לבין נמק, מוגלה ופצעים מרובים** מעורר חשד להזנחה. מדובר בסימן אזהרה המחייב בירור, לצד טיפול דחוף בזיהום.

**א. זיהום עם נוירופתיה.** זהו סיבוך מוכר של סוכרת גם בטיפול מסור.
**ב. אי־התאמה בין ההסבר לממצאים.** הפער מצדיק תיעוד, שיחה נפרדת ובחינת זמינות הטיפול והמשאבים.
**ג. HbA1c גבוה.** מעיד על איזון סוכר לקוי, אך אינו מוכיח מי אחראי לכך.
**ד. הזיהוי בידי עוזרת הבית.** עיתוי הזיהוי מוסיף הקשר, אך כשלעצמו פחות ממוקד מהפער הקליני.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, נוהל טיפול בזקנים נפגעי התעמרות, נספח 1.

q: A 78-year-old man with dementia and falls takes oxybutynin. The team decides to remove the strongly anticholinergic drug from his regimen and plan treatment of urinary incontinence separately. Which action achieves that aim?
o: Discontinue treatment with oxybutynin
Replace treatment with solifenacin
Replace treatment with tolterodine
Replace treatment with trospium
explanation:
Oxybutynin is a bladder antimuscarinic with strong anticholinergic properties. Other medicines in the same class can preserve that exposure when substituted.

**Discontinue oxybutynin and assess incontinence separately.** This achieves the team’s goal of removing a strong anticholinergic.

**A. Stop oxybutynin.** Withdrawal removes the current exposure without introducing another bladder antimuscarinic.
**B. Replace with solifenacin.** Solifenacin is also strongly anticholinergic.
**C. Replace with tolterodine.** Tolterodine continues muscarinic blockade and warrants cognitive caution.
**D. Replace with trospium.** Trospium also belongs to the strongly anticholinergic bladder drug group, even though individual agents differ.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2074.

. Replace with solifenacin.** Solifenacin is also strongly anticholinergic.
. Replace with tolterodine.** Tolterodine continues muscarinic blockade and warrants cognitive caution.
. Replace with trospium.** Trospium also belongs to the strongly anticholinergic bladder drug group, even though individual agents differ.

q: An 84-year-old man develops dizziness, falls, and an orthostatic blood pressure drop after starting tamsulosin. Initial evaluation finds no urinary retention, volume depletion, or acute cardiac cause. What is the appropriate initial medication approach?
o: Withdraw tamsulosin and reassess standing symptoms
Add midodrine during the day
Start low-dose fludrocortisone
Prescribe meclizine for dizziness
explanation:
A new alpha blocker can lower standing pressure by impeding vasoconstriction. **Withdraw tamsulosin and reassess** when symptomatic hypotension and falls begin after its introduction.

**A. Withdraw and reassess** — The time course and postural measurements support a trial of withdrawal. Follow urinary symptoms as well as falls.
**B. Continue and add midodrine** — An alpha agonist may help persistent severe hypotension, but it would be added while the suspected contributor remains.
**C. Continue and add fludrocortisone** — Volume expansion does not remove alpha blockade and introduces risks including edema and supine hypertension.
**D. Continue and add meclizine** — Meclizine is a vestibular suppressant. It cannot correct the pressure fall and may worsen balance.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 668, 675.

. Continue and add fludrocortisone** — Volume expansion does not remove alpha blockade and introduces risks including edema and supine hypertension.
. Continue and add meclizine** — Meclizine is a vestibular suppressant. It cannot correct the pressure fall and may worsen balance.

q: A 79-year-old man with advanced heart failure and additional comorbidities is referred for evaluation for a left ventricular assist device (LVAD). He is unsure whether it fits his goals. When does Hazzard recommend incorporating palliative care consultation?
o: When home inotropic therapy is selected after further deterioration
During evaluation for the device, to clarify goals of care
During follow-up after implantation, to assess adaptation to the device
When a device complication prompts reconsideration of treatment
explanation:
A durable LVAD can improve survival and function but entails major surgery, device care and possible complications. **Involve palliative care during LVAD evaluation** so his values can guide the decision itself.

**A. Wait for home inotropes** Inotropes represent another advanced or palliative option. Their use is not a prerequisite for consultation.
**B. Consult during evaluation** Explore what outcomes he would value, how device dependence fits his life and what support is available.
**C. Wait for postoperative follow-up** Adaptation matters after implantation, but that timing misses his present decision.
**D. Wait for a complication** Discuss possible burdens and future treatment preferences before the operation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1189–1190.

q: A 78-year-old woman who has never smoked has stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, brain metastases, and an EGFR L858R mutation. She takes amlodipine, metformin, and simvastatin, has reduced renal function, and lives independently but has stopped driving because of mild cognitive impairment. Which initial treatment is supported by the FLAURA results described in Hazzard, including improved overall survival and efficacy in CNS metastases?
o: Gefitinib
Osimertinib
Erlotinib
Carboplatin with pemetrexed
explanation:
EGFR L858R is a sensitizing mutation in lung adenocarcinoma. **Osimertinib** is the EGFR inhibitor associated in FLAURA with first-line survival benefit and activity in CNS metastases.

**A. Gefitinib.** This earlier-generation EGFR inhibitor was a comparator, not the agent providing the reported advantage.
**B. Osimertinib.** Its activity against sensitizing EGFR mutations and CNS disease fits this patient's mutation and brain metastases.
**C. Erlotinib.** It is another earlier-generation comparator in EGFR-mutant disease.
**D. Carboplatin and pemetrexed.** Cytotoxic chemotherapy does not exploit the identified actionable EGFR mutation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1427.

. Osimertinib.** Its activity against sensitizing EGFR mutations and CNS disease fits this patient's mutation and brain metastases.
. Erlotinib.** It is another earlier-generation comparator in EGFR-mutant disease.
. Carboplatin and pemetrexed.** Cytotoxic chemotherapy does not exploit the identified actionable EGFR mutation.

q: An 83-year-old woman with localized colorectal cancer, heart failure, and functional limitations is being assessed for treatment. No urgent intervention is currently needed. Which basis for decision-making follows the principles described for older adults with gastrointestinal malignancy?
o: Choose palliative treatment from chronological age and tumor type
Choose operative treatment from tumor stage and imaging findings
Choose palliative treatment from residence and the cancer diagnosis
Weigh treatment toxicity, comorbidity, and functional status
explanation:
Treatment planning for localized gastrointestinal cancer should weigh cancer benefit against patient reserve. **Assess expected toxicity, heart failure and functional status** before choosing an elective intervention.

**A. Age and tumor type alone.** Neither captures cardiac risk or ability to recover.
**B. Stage and imaging alone.** Resectability cannot predict an individual patient's perioperative or treatment tolerance.
**C. Residence and diagnosis alone.** Living arrangements do not measure functional reserve or goals.
**D. Balance toxicity, comorbidity and function.** These factors inform both treatment intensity and the practical consequences of recovery.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1435.

. Stage and imaging alone.** Resectability cannot predict an individual patient's perioperative or treatment tolerance.
. Residence and diagnosis alone.** Living arrangements do not measure functional reserve or goals.
. Balance toxicity, comorbidity and function.** These factors inform both treatment intensity and the practical consequences of recovery.

q: גבר בן 83 מתאר הופעה מהירה של קרטוזות סבוראיות רבות, גרד, ירידה במשקל ושובע מוקדם. בבירור התגלתה אדנוקרצינומה בקיבה. איזו גישה נותנת עדיפות לבעיה העיקרית לצד הקלה על הגרד?
o: להסתפק בהקפאת הנגעים ולדחות טיפול בגידול
להתחיל רטינואיד מקומי ולהמתין לתגובה עורית
לתאם טיפול בממאירות ולהציע הקלה מקומית לפי הצורך
להסיר את כל הנגעים לפני הערכה אונקולוגית
explanation:
נגעים המתפרצים במהירות עם תסמינים מערכתיים מצדיקים בירור לממאירות. כאן הגידול כבר אובחן. טיפול מקומי בנגעים מטרידים יכול להקל על הגרד במקביל לטיפול אונקולוגי.

**א. להסתפק בהקפאת הנגעים ולדחות טיפול בגידול** — אפשר לטפל בנגעים מטרידים, אך אין לדחות בשל כך את הטיפול בגידול.
**ב. להתחיל רטינואיד מקומי ולהמתין לתגובה עורית** — טיפול שדה מקומי אינו תחליף לטיפול בממאירות מאובחנת.
**ג. לתאם טיפול בממאירות ולהציע הקלה מקומית לפי הצורך** — הטיפול בגידול הוא בעדיפות, וניתן להקל על הגרד במקביל.
**ד. להסיר את כל הנגעים לפני הערכה אונקולוגית** — אין הצדקה להסרה נרחבת לפני הערכה אונקולוגית.

q: An 81-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia is admitted from assisted living for pneumonia. On day three, she becomes disoriented and tries to leave. She previously managed basic ADLs independently but now needs dressing assistance. She takes donepezil 10 mg, sertraline 50 mg, and IV ceftriaxone. Vital signs are stable; WBC is 14,000, creatinine 0.9, and electrolytes normal. While assessing acute precipitants, which initial symptom-management approach fits Hazzard?
o: Start quetiapine before trying reorientation and family support
Increase donepezil to address the acute disorientation
Stop sertraline without reviewing other potential precipitants
Arrange family support, reorientation, and supervision
explanation:
Pneumonia and unfamiliar surroundings can trigger distress and disorientation in a patient with Alzheimer dementia. Family can help distinguish baseline from the new episode and guide reassurance.
**Bring in familiar support, repeat orienting cues and supervise her safely while treating acute contributors.**

**A. Start quetiapine before trying reorientation and family support.** There is no indication to give quetiapine before trying support and reorientation in a stable patient.
**B. Increase donepezil to address the acute disorientation.** Donepezil is chronic symptomatic dementia therapy, not an acute delirium intervention.
**C. Stop sertraline without reviewing other potential precipitants.** Review all medicines and their timing before assigning causation to a longstanding drug.
**D. Arrange family support, reorientation, and supervision.** Familiar contact and observation address distress and attempts to leave without clouding attention.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 887–888, Table 58-5

q: מה המשפט המתאר בצורה נכונה את יעילות טיפולים לא תרופתיים באוסטאוארטריטיס?
o: ירידה במשקל עוזרת רק בירידה של מעל 10% מהמשקל
קירור מקומי עם קרח יעיל בהפחתת כאב ודלקת אם הטיפול נמשך 30 דקות לפחות בכל פעם
יש להדריך את החולה להשתמש במקל הליכה ביד של אותו צד של הרגל הפגועה
שימוש בסד ברך (knee brace ) מייצב את הברך ומונע נפילות
explanation:
Non-drug treatment can change how load passes through an unstable knee. **A properly selected brace improves stability and may reduce falls** in someone whose knee gives way.

**A. Weight loss helps only beyond ten percent** — Benefits can begin at about five percent in overweight people with knee or hip OA. Greater loss may give greater benefit.
**B. Ice for at least thirty minutes** — Limit a cold application to about twenty minutes and protect the skin to reduce injury from prolonged exposure.
**C. Cane on the affected side** — Hold the cane opposite the painful hip or knee. Advancing it with the affected leg helps off-load that side.
**D. Knee brace** — Tibiofemoral bracing can improve stability and walking in varus or valgus instability. Improvement reduces risk without guaranteeing that falls will cease.

Reference · June 2022 exam bibliography, Hazzard 7e, pp. 1795–1796. Corresponding topic in Hazzard 8e, pp. 785–787.

q: בן 75, דייר מחלקה סיעודית. ברקע דמנציה וסקולרית. מזה כחודש פצע לחץ, כעת בדרגה 3 בטרוכנטר שמאל. משקל 60 ק"ג, BMI 20. בחודש האחרון ירד במשקל כ-4.5 ק"ג. הפצע מטופל מקומית בחבישות מתקדמות. מה מהבאים עשוי לשפר את ריפוי הפצע?
o: ויטמין C 1000 מ"ג ליום
ויטמין E 200 מ"ג ליום
LEUCIN 400 מ"ג ליום
חלבון 90 גר' ליום
explanation:
Loss of 4.5 kg in a month raises concern for insufficient energy and protein during wound repair. Translate a weight-based target into the patient's actual daily intake.

**For a 60-kg patient, 90 g of protein/day is 1.5 g/kg/day.** It reaches the upper end of the 1.3–1.5 g/kg/day healing range and should be accompanied by adequate energy.

**A. Vitamin C 1,000 mg.** High-dose vitamin C alone lacks a demonstrated healing benefit in a person without a specific deficiency and leaves protein intake unaddressed.
**B. Vitamin E 200 mg.** Additional vitamin E is not a replacement for protein-energy repletion in a patient losing weight.
**C. Leucine 400 mg.** A small amount of one amino acid cannot supply the complete daily protein target.
**D. Protein 90 g/day.** The calculated range is 78–90 g/day at this weight. Assess tolerability, actual intake and the energy available to support healing.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 692.

q: Which drug class remains the treatment of choice for delirium caused by seizures or alcohol/medication withdrawal, despite not being first-line for delirium generally?
o: Melatonin receptor agonists
Antipsychotics
Benzodiazepines
Alpha-2 agonists
explanation:
Sedatives may worsen ordinary delirium, but withdrawal and seizures have a different treatment mechanism. Benzodiazepines can control withdrawal-related excitation and seizure activity.
**A benzodiazepine treats ongoing seizure activity or delirium from alcohol or sedative-hypnotic withdrawal.** Establish the specific drug and withdrawal syndrome before choosing treatment.

**A. Melatonin receptor agonists.** Trials of melatonin agents in delirium have mixed results and they do not treat withdrawal seizures.
**B. Antipsychotics.** Antipsychotics may control selected dangerous behaviors but do not treat a withdrawal syndrome.
**C. Benzodiazepines.** Enhancing inhibitory GABA signaling can stop an active seizure and counter the hyperexcitability of alcohol or sedative withdrawal. Other withdrawal syndromes require their own treatment.
**D. Alpha-2 agonists.** Dexmedetomidine can be an ICU adjunct in resistant alcohol withdrawal but does not protect against withdrawal seizures. Clonidine or lofexidine can relieve autonomic symptoms of opioid withdrawal, a different syndrome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 889. ASAM Alcohol Withdrawal Management, VI.13–14. ASAM National Practice Guideline for Opioid Use Disorder, 2020 focused update, Part 3.

q: What gene mutation, discovered in 2011, is the major cause of familial FTD, ALS, and FTD-ALS?
o: VCP (valosin-containing protein)
Progranulin
C9orf72
MAPT
explanation:
The 2011 discovery was a **C9orf72 hexanucleotide repeat expansion**. A single family can include members with ALS, frontotemporal dementia or both.

**A. Valosin-containing protein.** VCP variants can cause multisystem proteinopathy with FTD, myopathy and Paget disease.
**B. Progranulin.** GRN variants commonly cause inherited FTLD with TDP-43 pathology. They are a different genetic cause.
**C. C9orf72.** Expansion of a noncoding repeat links chromosome 9p to familial ALS and FTD.
**D. MAPT.** MAPT mutations cause inherited tau-associated FTD, often with parkinsonism.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 63, p. 990. Renton et al., Neuron 2011, PMID 21944779.

q: What fraction of non-constipated older adults fail to expel a test sphere on simulated defecation testing?
explanation:
Expelling a test sphere requires coordinated abdominal propulsion and pelvic-floor relaxation. An abnormal simulated test can occur even without reported constipation.
**Thirty-seven percent of non-constipated older participants could not expel the sphere.**

**A. Thirty-seven percent.** More than one in three failed, so interpret a single abnormal result with symptoms and other findings.
**B. Seven percent.** This markedly understates failure in the asymptomatic group.
**C. Fourteen percent.** This is also well below the observed fraction.
**D. Thirteen percent.** The observed frequency of failed expulsion was closer to one in three than one in eight.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1357.

q: An older outpatient has primary hyperparathyroidism caused by a single parathyroid adenoma. Which process explains this disorder?
o: Compensatory PTH secretion in response to low serum calcium
Autonomous PTH secretion from abnormal parathyroid tissue
Parathyroid hyperplasia after longstanding severe secondary hyperparathyroidism
Specimen acidosis during delayed processing of an ionized-calcium sample
explanation:
A parathyroid adenoma releases PTH despite calcium concentrations that should suppress it. **Autonomous PTH secretion is the mechanism of primary hyperparathyroidism.**

**A. Compensation for low calcium** — This is secondary hyperparathyroidism, as can occur with vitamin D deficiency.
**B. Autonomous secretion** — A single adenoma is the most common cause. PTH can be elevated or inappropriately within the laboratory range during hypercalcemia.
**C. Hyperplasia after prolonged secondary disease** — This describes tertiary hyperparathyroidism, commonly following advanced chronic kidney disease.
**D. Sample acidosis** — Incorrect handling can alter measured ionized calcium. It cannot create chronic autonomous PTH secretion.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1536–1538.

o: ב- MALLORY-WEISS TEARS -> טיפול ב- SOMATOSTATIN תוך ורידי
בכיב עם דמם פעיל -> צריבה או הזרקה לכלי הדם
בכיב עם קריש צמוד -> אין מקום לטיפול אנדוסקופי
בדליות -> טיפול ב- CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKERS

explanation:
The endoscopic lesion determines hemostatic treatment in upper GI bleeding. **An actively bleeding peptic ulcer needs endoscopic hemostasis**, typically mechanical or thermal treatment, with injection used as an adjunct when appropriate.

**A. Intravenous somatostatin for a Mallory-Weiss tear.** Most Mallory–Weiss tears stop spontaneously. Persistent bleeding can be treated endoscopically; IV somatostatin is not the defining treatment.
**B. Thermal or injection treatment for an actively bleeding ulcer.** Treat the bleeding vessel. Dilute epinephrine injection by itself should not be mistaken for adequate definitive ulcer therapy.
**C. No endoscopic treatment for an adherent ulcer clot.** An adherent clot may warrant irrigation and assessment or treatment of the underlying lesion. The absolute claim that endoscopy has no role is wrong.
**D. Calcium-channel blockers for varices.** Variceal bleeding calls for vasoactive therapy and endoscopic treatment, not calcium-channel blockade.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 317–318.

chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 75 – Prevention and Early Detection of Cancer
keySource: IMA 2023-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q150
explanation:
CT colonography images the colon and surrounding organs, so **unrelated extracolonic findings can trigger additional investigations**. Some of those findings never become clinically important.

**A. FOBT plus sigmoidoscopy equals colonoscopy.** The tests differ in the bowel they assess and the advanced lesions they detect. Combining two tests does not guarantee identical performance.
**B. CT performs less well for small lesions.** Sensitivity falls as polyp size decreases. Small lesions can be missed even when larger lesions are readily seen.
**C. Incidental findings.** Imaging outside the bowel can lead to follow-up imaging or procedures for uncertain abnormalities.
**D. FOBT has no mortality benefit.** Trials of repeated fecal occult blood screening have shown reduced colorectal-cancer mortality.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 517–518. de Haan et al., Diagnostic value of CT-colonography as compared to colonoscopy in an asymptomatic screening population, Table 2.
Key note: With colonoscopy as the reference, pooled CT-colonography sensitivity was lower for 6–9 mm polyps than for polyps at least 10 mm. This gives clinical support to the small-lesion option as well as the incidental-finding answer.
